main_text.l: ISAACI CASAVBONI AD
THEOPHRASTI CHARA-
CTERES ETHICOS
Liber Commentarius.
[?]ΔΗ μὲν καὶ πρότερον πολλάκις.] Ostendit Theophrastus, non imparatum se
ad huius operis scriptionem accede-
re: sed re saepius secum considerata,
expensaque. Ideo ait ὅτι σημαίνας τὸν
διά-νοιαν[?]: familiari Aristoteli, & aliis philosophis lo-
quendi genere. simplicius Xenophon initio Παι-δείας[?], Ἔννοια ποτὲ ἡμῖν
ἐγχωρεῖ[?]. & initio Commentariorum, Πολλάκις ἐθαύμασα[?]. At noster mox quoque
verbis significantissimis vtitur, σωθεωρήσας[?], &
ἀπαγγελτικῶ[?]: quae dictiones, Θεάσαι inquam, &
Θεωρῶν[?], à rebus diuinis originem habentes, de quibus
dum attentius meditamur, fimus ipsi quodammo-
do diuini, & vt philosophus ait in decimo Nico-
macheorum, nos ipsos ἀπαθανατίζομεν[?]: postea ad
eas res sunt translatae, quas cum magna voluptate,
vel magna cum attentione contemplamur. Eôdem
spectat & quod ait, ὁμοιωθῆναι πανταχῶς
ἀνθρώ-πων φύσειν[?]: fuit enim necesse vt qui describere ho-
minum

page.notes: The large initial H (lines 2 to 4 of the paragraph) is a decorated letter; I could not match it to a joined word, so it is not reproduced as a separate word. Greek lines are small and partly smudged: all Greek is copied as best seen and marked [?] throughout, with the hyphenated Greek word split at the line end ("διά-νοιαν", "ἀνθρώ-πων"). The paragraph continues onto the next page after "ho-minum". A stray mark in the left margin and a mark at the foot of the page are not printed text and are left out.
